messages:
anna (oncall): Pager triggered for high OOM rate on decode-stream nodes in us-west-2, multiple container restarts reported. Noticing lots of long-running streaming calls.
sam (sre): seeing CUDA OOM logs on node gpu-decode-47: \"cudaErrorOutOfMemory: out of memory during kernel launch\". Crash loop started ~2m ago.
mike (runtime): looking at serving logs — heavy tail on requests with unbounded generation. Client header shows \"max_tokens:\" missing for many requests. suspect SDK default change.
lisa (support): a customer (acct: acme-corp) reported 50% request drop rate and partial responses. Raising customer impact.
pagerbot: Incident created: INC-2026-2247. Priority: P1. Notifying oncall roster.
anna (oncall): quick plan: 1) enable decode-throttle circuit breaker on affected pool, 2) enforce max_tokens on edge (fail closed), 3) pin fallback model to smaller LLM. Sam/mike take 1/2.
sam (sre): applying temporary iptables throttle to reduce concurrency to gpu-decode-*. will push a traffic rule now.
mike (runtime): rolling config to set request-level max_tokens=512 for all streaming endpoints in us-west-2 (hotpatch). Command:

```
redwoodctl rollout set-config --env us-west-2 --route streaming.decode --defaults "{\"max_tokens\":512}" --force
```

deploy-bot: Rollout started: roll-2026-6112. 10% -> 100% over 3m.
sam (sre): node gpu-decode-47 still OOM'ing after throttle; container restarted again. Investigating kernel stack.
mike (runtime): digging into decoder kernel traces — runaway attention kv growth on long prompts plus repeated prefix caching. One request had token-count reported as 2.1M (buggy tokenization metric). That explains OOM.
lisa (support): customer update: "We're seeing truncated completions and timeouts, started ~12:08 PT". Want ETA.
anna (oncall): ETA 15m to stabilize with rollouts + model fallback. Notify customers and ops.
mike (runtime): enabling model fallback policy: route requests over 128k tokens to a mem-constrained variant and reject > 256k. Command:

```
redwoodctl policy set fallback --pool decode-usw --when "token_count > 128000" --to small-decode-v1
```

pagerbot: Fallback policy applied.
sam (sre): observed immediate drop in OOM frequency after throttle + config, node pool stabilized. Still seeing stragglers from long-lived streams.
mike (runtime): pushing patch to tokenizer that clamps max_tokens header parsing to humane values and emits metric 'client_max_tokens_parsed'. Patch id: rt-2026-451.
anna (oncall): good. Can we also roll a temporary rate-limit per-API-key to stop runaway clients?
mike (runtime): added per-key soft quota 100 reqs/min for hosts with >2k concurrent tokens. Should throttle noisy clients.
lisa (support): telling acme-corp: "We've applied protective throttles and fallbacks; your traffic should be stabilized. We're still investigating root cause and will follow up with logs and mitigation timeline. Apologies for the disruption." Customer asked for postmortem.
sam (sre): note: there were also a pair of node flaps coincident with a driver upgrade on node pool yesterday (kernel 6.1.14 -> 6.1.15). I/O scheduler warnings align with GPU driver rebinds.
mike (runtime): for remediation: (a) add pre-check to reject absurd token counts at edge, (b) backfill a canary to validate SDK default change, (c) add KV cache TTL to limit growth per-stream.
anna (oncall): handoff to oncall-night in 45m. I'll file a followup ticket for a deeper postmortem: includes cust impact, timeline, root cause (SDK header parsing + driver/kv growth synergy). Assign to runtime + infra.
pagerbot: On-call handoff scheduled to anna-night at 2026-03-15T03:00:00Z.
sam (sre): in case note: saved heap dump from gpu-decode-47: /var/log/oom-dumps/gpu-decode-47-6112233456.dump
mike (runtime): adding alert: token_count > 500k triggers Pager. New rule id: alert-rt-500k.
lisa (support): customer follow-up logged: SUP-86422. Will send status update once we confirm full recovery.
anna (oncall): closing incident once 30m stable and no new OOMs. Current status: mitigations applied, customer notified, actions logged. :white_check_mark:
